summary: The user links two sessions on one backend with /link <session> [messages] (one chat may hold any number of links; each is an edge, and /link has the /send-to chat picker). Agent sends along a link skip the one-hop limit and the per-sender budget and spend the edge's own budget (the chosen 1 to 200 messages, default 20, or 30 minutes, renewed by a message the user types in either session or sends along the edge; Extend adds 20 and restarts the window). Sends anywhere else keep every existing limit. Auto mode sends along a link without a card. A spent link refuses as tool output telling the agent the message was not delivered and to keep working and report it, stores the message in the sender's chat as a Not delivered row with Send, and notifies once by push and desktop notification. A paired phone may unlink but never link or extend. Stop or archive removes a link; links are in memory only. list_agent_sessions marks linked sessions, and the desktop shows a compact banner with Extend and Unlink.

reactNativeIos.followUpRelease: mobile-v0.6.0. The phone neither creates nor extends links (refused for its chat scope in device-auth.ts, by design) and shows no banner or Not delivered row yet. Nothing unfinished is reachable: the React Native client calls none of the new channels, ignores provider:peer-links-changed and the new peer.undelivered event (its reducer has a default branch), and does not render system rows, so the stored Not delivered marker never appears raw. What it already gets: the link-spent push (kind 'link', routed by threadId like every other push) and the ordinary peer-message rows for linked exchanges. The follow-up adds the banner with Unlink, which the phone scope already allows.

nativeAndroid.followUpRelease: Native Android 0.6.0. Same as the React Native client: no linking or extending (refused for the phone scope), no banner or Not delivered row yet, and peer.undelivered decodes as an Extension event that nothing renders. The link-spent push carries kind 'link'; RemotePushNotificationPolicy only builds its own completion notification for 'done', so whether the system shows this one in the Android app is unverified (see notExercised).

updateRelease.reason: No package identity, signing, deep link, update channel or wire-frame change. provider:link-peer, provider:extend-peer-link, provider:unlink-peer and provider:list-peer-links are additive request/response channels; a desktop pointed at an older backend gets the unknown-channel error, which /link shows in the composer and the banner logs and hides. provider:peer-links-changed is a broadcast older clients never subscribe to, and peer.undelivered is a new RuntimeEvent older clients drop (desktop reducer and React Native default branches, Android Extension kind). The Not delivered row is an ordinary system message with a [[sb: prefix, so it reloads through the existing getSystemMarkerMessages path with no schema change; an older desktop renders it as a plain system line. The new push kind 'link' is routed by threadId like the others.

automated: tests/unit/peer-links.test.ts: link lifecycle; an agent cannot link or extend; a hub with three and with ten edges, workers not linked; budgets per edge, chosen budget 1 to 200 (0, 201, 1.5 refused), kept across renewals; exhaustion and expiry; refusal text says NOT delivered, keep working, final reply; first refusal reported once until renewed; renewal by a human message in either session or by a user send along the edge; Extend adds 20, restarts the window, caps at 200 and refuses at the cap when spent; release; the third-session hop limit; banner text for two and for ten links (with the used-up count); the undelivered marker round trip, broken rows, stable ids and heading.

tests/unit/peer-links-registry-ws.test.ts against the real registry over WsHost: linking needs both sessions live and broadcasts; list_agent_sessions marks linked sessions; a hub fans out past the per-sender budget, and to ten workers; workers still cannot message each other; a linked session at depth > 0 still cannot reach an unlinked one; 20 messages exhaust an edge and a human turn renews it; a spent link stores each refused message in the sender's chat and publishes peer.undelivered with notify only on the first; Send (a user delivery with undeliveredId) delivers it, renews the edge and marks the row sent; a chosen budget and the 200 bound over the wire; Extend over the wire; unlink, stop and archive; requireLink after an unlink.

tests/unit/peer-links-registry-ws.test.ts, 'a link changing while the send is prepared': an unlink during the checkpoint await delivers nothing, keeps a link-removed Not delivered row without a notification and frees the per-pair slot; an unlink and relink there is a different edge whose budget stays unspent; a target removed there gets the link charge refunded. Each of those fails with the re-check or the refund removed. peer-links.test.ts: a charge is refunded only to the edge that took it.
tests/unit/push-policy.test.ts: the link-spent push names both sessions, kind 'link', once (not for notify:false or a sent row).
tests/unit/device-auth.test.ts: a phone scope cannot call provider:link-peer or provider:extend-peer-link, and can call provider:unlink-peer and provider:list-peer-links.
tests/unit/mcp-peer-tools.test.ts: the card rules by mode, and the server exposes no link tool.

tests/unit/link-command.test.ts and send-to-command.test.ts: /link budget parsing, a chat titled 'Issue 172' stays reachable, out-of-range budgets refused, picker trigger for /link (closed while the budget is typed), pinning a picked title with its budget.
npm run typecheck and npm test green.
notExercised: Not run against live Claude, Codex or OpenCode sessions: no real agent pair was driven through a linked back-and-forth, so how each model uses the reply path and the not-delivered instruction is untested.

The banner (Extend, Manage popover with ten links), the Not delivered row and its Send button, the /link picker and the desktop notification were not exercised in the running app or by an e2e; the visual screens do not include a linked chat.
No push was sent to a real phone. Whether the native Android app displays a kind 'link' push (its RemotePushNotificationPolicy special-cases only 'done') is unverified.
